subject: ss-cardiology
title: Cyanotic and adult congenital heart disease: anatomy, repaired physiology and late complications

steps.tx: **Tetralogy of Fallot** consists of 4 classic anatomical components resulting from anterior and cephalad deviation of the infundibular septum: large malaligned perimembranous VSD, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction (infundibular and valvular pulmonic stenosis), overriding aorta (< 50%), and concentric right ventricular hypertrophy.
steps.say: Tetralogy of Fallot consists of four anatomical components resulting from anterocephalad deviation of the outlet septum: a large malaligned ventricular septal defect, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, an overriding aorta, and concentric right ventricular hypertrophy. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

rows: Determines the direction and degree of shunt
Directly receives mixed systemic and venous blood
Secondary to chronic RV outflow obstruction

steps.tx: Late complications in repaired adult TOF are driven by chronic severe **pulmonary regurgitation** following transannular patch repair. Guidelines recommend **pulmonary valve replacement** prior to irreversible RV damage when RV end-diastolic volume index exceeds 160 mL/m2 or end-systolic volume index exceeds 80 mL/m2 on cardiac MRI.
steps.say: Late complications in repaired adult Tetralogy of Fallot are dominated by chronic pulmonary regurgitation. Guidelines recommend timely pulmonary valve replacement before irreversible dysfunction develops, indicated when right ventricular end-diastolic volume index exceeds 160 millilitres per square metre. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

rows: Prevents irreversible RV remodeling and failure
Threshold for postoperative RV functional recovery
Relieves annular dilatation from RV enlargement

steps.tx: The magnetic resonance panels show a markedly enlarged right ventricle labelled **severely dilated RV** beside a small left ventricle, with the prior **VSD patch** visible at the septum. The outflow view shows a dark **severe pulmonary regurgitation** jet filling the outflow tract. Because chronic volume load drives irreversible dysfunction, meeting the lesson volume threshold makes timely **pulmonary valve replacement** the key referral decision.
steps.say: The MRI shows a severely dilated right ventricle with a VSD patch and a prominent pulmonary regurgitation jet, the expected late picture after transannular patch repair. Recognizing this degree of enlargement matters because once indexed volumes cross the guideline threshold, pulmonary valve replacement before irreversible damage is the treatment that preserves function.

steps.tx: **Eisenmenger syndrome** represents the irreversible end-stage consequence of uncorrected congenital systemic-to-pulmonary shunts (VSD, PDA, ASD). Progressive pulmonary arteriolar plexiform remodeling elevates pulmonary vascular resistance above systemic resistance, causing **shunt reversal** to right-to-left, central cyanosis, and secondary erythrocytosis. Clinical mastery requires rigorous recognition of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria.
steps.say: Eisenmenger syndrome represents the irreversible progression of uncorrected congenital left-to-right shunts into severe plexiform pulmonary arteriopathy. Pulmonary vascular resistance rises above systemic vascular resistance, precipitating shunt reversal to right-to-left and central cyanosis. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

steps.tx: **Differential cyanosis**, with pink upper extremities and cyanotic clubbed lower extremities, is pathognomonic of patent ductus arteriosus complicated by Eisenmenger physiology. Deoxygenated blood shunting right-to-left from the pulmonary artery traverses the ductus into the descending aorta distal to the left subclavian artery take-off.
steps.say: Differential cyanosis, characterized by normal pink upper extremities and cyanotic clubbed toes, is pathognomonic of patent ductus arteriosus with Eisenmenger physiology. Deoxygenated blood enters the descending aorta distal to the left subclavian artery, sparing the cerebral and upper extremity circulations.

left.title: Upper Extremities
points: Pink fingernails, normal oxygen saturation; perfusing blood originates from aortic arch proximal to ductal insertion.

right.title: Lower Extremities
points: Cyanotic, clubbed toes, reduced oxygen saturation; perfusing blood receives right-to-left deoxygenated ductal shunt.

steps.tx: **Transposition of the great arteries** (d-TGA) features ventriculoarterial discordance, where the aorta arises from the morphological right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the morphological left ventricle. The neonatal surgical anatomical repair of choice is the **arterial switch** operation (Jatene procedure) with coronary button reimplantation.
steps.say: D-transposition of the great arteries features ventriculoarterial discordance with parallel circulations. The aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the left ventricle. The neonatal surgical repair of choice is the arterial switch operation with coronary reimplantation.

rows: Translocates great vessels and coronaries; restores LV as systemic pump
Baffles caval and pulmonary flow; leaves RV as systemic ventricle
High incidence of late arrhythmias and RV failure

steps.tx: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (l-TGA) is defined by **double discordance**: atrioventricular discordance and ventriculoarterial discordance. Systemic venous blood reaches the lungs while pulmonary venous blood reaches the aorta, but the morphological RV serves as the **systemic RV failure** chamber, prone to complete AV block.
steps.say: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries features double discordance, combining atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance. Because the morphological right ventricle supports the systemic circulation, long-term complications include systemic right ventricular failure and high-grade AV block. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

left.title: Double Discordance
points: RA to morphological LV to PA; LA to morphological RV to Aorta; hemodynamically physiologically corrected circulation.

right.title: Long-Term Failure
points: Morphological systemic RV lacks three-layered architecture, developing progressive systolic failure and systemic tricuspid regurgitation.

steps.tx: The **Fontan procedure** provides palliation for single-ventricle anatomies by routing systemic venous blood directly to the pulmonary arteries without a subpulmonary pump. Chronic nonpulsatile pulmonary flow causes elevated central venous pressure, leading to late multiorgan complications including **protein-losing enteropathy**, plastic bronchitis, and cirrhosis.
steps.say: The Fontan procedure provides palliation for single ventricle anatomies by routing systemic venous blood directly into the pulmonary arteries. Chronic absence of a subpulmonary pump leads to elevated venous pressures, predisposing to protein-losing enteropathy, plastic bronchitis, and Fontan-associated liver disease.

rows: Enteric albumin loss; elevated fecal alpha-1-antitrypsin
Lymphatic congestion weeping into bronchial tree
Chronic sinusoidal congestion and parenchymal fibrosis
Atrial flutter, IART, sinus node failure
Right atrial surgical scarring and stretch

steps.tx: **Secondary erythrocytosis** in cyanotic CHD is a physiologic compensation for chronic tissue hypoxemia, maintaining tissue oxygen delivery. Therapeutic phlebotomy is indicated only for acute symptomatic **hyperviscosity** when hematocrit > 65% in the absence of dehydration, accompanied by equal-volume crystalloid replacement to avoid microvascular stroke.
steps.say: Secondary erythrocytosis in cyanotic heart disease represents a compensatory response to chronic hypoxemia. Therapeutic phlebotomy is indicated strictly for symptomatic hyperviscosity when hematocrit exceeds 65 percent in the absence of dehydration, accompanied by equal volume crystalloid repletion. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

left.title: Compensated Erythrocytosis
points: High hematocrit, normal microcytosis, asymptomatic; maintains essential peripheral tissue oxygen delivery.

right.title: Decompensated Hyperviscosity
points: Hematocrit > 65%, headache, visual blurring, fatigue; requires gentle phlebotomy with concurrent volume replacement.
